name: Subject Body Mask
systemPrompt:
Create a minimalist magazine-cover editorial collage using {{subjectImage}} as the main portrait subject and {{overlayImage}} as a silhouette-based photographic texture layer.

### INPUT REFERENCES:
Use {{subjectImage}} only for the identity, facial structure, hairstyle, expression, clothing, body proportions, and recognizable characteristics of the main subject.

Use {{overlayImage}} only as a visual image layer applied inside the subject’s body silhouette below the head area.

Do not copy the identity or content of any person from the style reference. The style reference controls only the aesthetic, composition, graphic treatment, and visual language.

### SUBJECT PRESERVATION:
Place the subject large and centered, cropped from the chest up.

Preserve the subject’s exact identity, facial structure, hairstyle, expression, clothing details, accessories, and natural proportions.

Keep the face completely clean, sharp, and unobstructed as the main focal point.

Convert the portrait into a high-contrast black-and-white editorial photograph with deep matte shadows, compressed highlights, and subtle printed grain.

### COMPOSITION:
Create a vertical editorial magazine-cover composition.

Position the subject as the dominant foreground element, occupying most of the frame.

Keep the head and facial area fully visible in monochrome.

Apply the overlay treatment only to the subject’s lower body and clothing silhouette, stopping naturally below the head.

The overlay should remain contained within the subject’s existing silhouette and should not extend outside the body shape.

### BACKGROUND TREATMENT:
Use a warm off-white minimal background with a subtle paper-like surface.

Place large bold abstract red geometric shapes behind the subject.

Arrange these shapes diagonally and asymmetrically to frame the portrait and create strong graphic contrast.

Keep the background clean, spacious, and refined with minimal texture.

### SILHOUETTE OVERLAY TREATMENT:
Use {{overlayImage}} to replace and mask the lower portion of the subject’s body and clothing area while preserving the original silhouette.

The overlay image should fit naturally inside the subject’s body shape like a photographic double exposure or editorial collage mask.

Do not create torn-paper edges, cutout fragments, paper folds, ripped textures, or collage pieces.

The overlay should feel like the subject’s clothing/body has been filled with another documentary image.

Apply {{overlayTintColor}} as a controlled color tint over the overlay image only.

Keep the overlay mostly monochrome with subtle color influence and a few stronger accent areas.

Add light photographic noise and grain to the overlay so it integrates with the printed editorial style.

Do not add heavy paper texture, distressed surfaces, or excessive ink damage over the overlay.

### STYLE MATCHING:
Match the visual language of a modern political magazine cover:

- realistic black-and-white portrait photography
- bold red geometric graphic background
- minimalist editorial composition
- documentary collage aesthetic
- controlled double exposure effect
- subtle print texture
- refined screen-print influence

The image should look like a professionally designed magazine cover combining photography, graphic design, and editorial collage.

### COLOUR TREATMENT:
The portrait head and visible face must remain pure black-and-white grayscale.

The overlay section must receive {{overlayTintColor}} as a clear but controlled tint.

The colour separation between the subject’s face and the overlay body treatment is mandatory and must be visually obvious at a glance.

### LIGHTING AND TONAL TREATMENT:
Use strong editorial contrast with defined facial shadows and clean highlights.

Keep the face sharper and more detailed than all surrounding elements.

Maintain a realistic photographic appearance with subtle print compression.

### TEXTURE AND FINISHING:
Add fine monochrome grain, slight print noise, and subtle photographic texture across the image.

Keep the background texture minimal.

Keep the overlay image clean with only light noise and tint integration.

Avoid excessive paper aging, scratches, distressed effects, or rough collage artifacts.

### STRICT REQUIREMENTS:
- No text
- No logos
- No typography
- No extra people
- No torn paper
- No paper cutouts
- No collage fragments outside the silhouette
- No overlay covering the face or head
- No identity changes
- No unrealistic body distortion

### AVOID:
Avoid heavy vintage damage.

Avoid excessive paper texture.

Avoid making the overlay look like a pasted object.

Avoid full-image color grading.

Avoid illustration, painting, or 3D rendering.

Avoid changing the subject’s facial details.
